requirements.title: Automatic stack link
requirements.rationale: An agent that pushes one branch on top of another expects the hub to see the stack without being told.

criteria.condition: package 22 calls LinkVersion of its StackLinker interface, which this package implements, for a version it records for a draft or open change that has no explicit depends_on for that version, and the current head of at least one other draft or open change of the same workspace with the same target branch is a proper ancestor of the new head
criteria.action: set the change's depends_on to the nearest such change (the one with the fewest commits between its head and the new head) and the version's base_sha to that change's head, both through the setters of package 22
criteria.contract: the change object has depends_on equal to the lower change's number and base_sha equal to the lower change's head_sha

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over {B opened on top of A; C opened on top of B on top of A (C must link to B, not A); A in state draft and B open; A's source in the target workspace and B's source in a fork of it; B at version 1 and B at a later pushed version}: record the version through the version recording of package 22; assert change.depends_on == number of the nearest lower change; assert change.base_sha == that change's head_sha

criteria.condition: a version is recorded for a draft or open change and no other draft or open change with the same target branch has a current head that is a proper ancestor of the new head
criteria.action: clear the change's depends_on and set the version's base_sha to the merge base of the new head and the target branch
criteria.contract: the change object has depends_on null and base_sha equal to the merge base with the target branch

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over {a first change on main; B that depended on A and is then force-pushed directly onto main}: record the version; assert change.depends_on == null; assert change.base_sha == mergeBase(head, main); for the second row assert A.dependants does not contain B

criteria.action: for any version it records, never choose as depends_on a change that is landed or abandoned, a change with another target branch, a change of another workspace, or a change whose head equals the new head, and choose the lowest number when two candidates share the nearest head
criteria.contract: depends_on names only a draft or open change of the same workspace and target branch whose head is a proper ancestor of the change's head

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over the lower candidate {landed, abandoned, open with target branch release while the new change targets main, open in another workspace whose repository holds the same commits, open with the same head as the new version}: record a version on top of the candidate's head; assert change.depends_on == null. One more row: changes 3 and 5 are open with the same head, a new change is pushed on top of it; assert depends_on == 3

criteria.action: for any link it sets or clears, store it through the depends_on setter of package 22, so that the dependants package 22 derives for every change list exactly the draft and open changes whose depends_on is that change
criteria.contract: dependants on the change object (rendered by package 22): array of integers, ascending, [] when there is none; this package keeps no second list of dependants

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go: A with B and C both opened on top of A, and D on top of B; assert A.dependants == [B, C]; assert B.dependants == [D]; assert D.dependants == []; abandon C through the store; assert A.dependants == [B]

criteria.action: for any dependent change, compute stats and paths of the current version from the commits after base_sha only, so that they cover the change's own commits and none of the change below
criteria.contract: stats.commits equals the number of commits after the lower change's head; paths lists only files those commits touch

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go: A has 2 commits touching a.txt; B is opened on top of A with 1 commit touching b.txt; assert B.stats.commits == 1; assert B.stats.files_changed == 1; assert B.paths == ['b.txt']

requirements.title: Explicit depends_on
requirements.rationale: A caller sometimes knows the order of its changes before the commit graph shows it, and must be told when the order it asks for is impossible.

criteria.condition: a caller sends depends_on with the number of a draft or open change of the same workspace and target branch, in the body of POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes or of PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number, and the link would not form a cycle
criteria.action: set the change's depends_on to that number and, when the lower change's head is an ancestor of the change's head, set base_sha to that head and recompute stats and paths against it
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 (open) or 200 (PATCH) with the change object carrying depends_on equal to the given number

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go with httptest, a table over {POST …/changes with depends_on: A for a branch built on A; PATCH B with depends_on: A where B is built on A's head and its link was cleared before by PATCH depends_on: null; PATCH B with depends_on: A where B is built on main only}: assert status == 201 or 200; assert json.depends_on == A.number; where B is built on A assert json.base_sha == A.head_sha; assert GET A .dependants contains B

criteria.condition: the depends_on sent at open or by PATCH names a change number that does not exist in the workspace, the change itself, a change whose own stack contains the change (a cycle), a change with a different target branch, or a change that is not draft or open
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing: no change is created at open, and no field of an existing change is modified
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_dependency, returned as an error from LinkVersion (open) or SetDependsOn (the PATCH of package 23), whose transaction is rolled back; the stored change (or the count of changes, at open) is unchanged

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go with httptest, a table over the value {999 (unknown), the change's own number, a change that depends on this one directly, a change that depends on this one through one change in between, a change targeting release, a landed change, an abandoned change} and the route {PATCH; POST …/changes for the rows that apply at open}: r = request; assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_dependency'; assert the stored change equals its state before the request, or count(changes) is unchanged; one row sends title together with the invalid depends_on and asserts the title is unchanged

criteria.condition: a caller sends PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number with depends_on null on a change that has a depends_on
criteria.action: clear the link, set base_sha to the merge base of the change's head and the target branch, and recompute stats and paths against it
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the change object carrying depends_on null; the former lower change's dependants no longer lists the change

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go with httptest: B depends on A; r = PATCH B {depends_on: null}; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.depends_on == null; assert r.json.base_sha == mergeBase(B.head, main); assert r.json.stats.commits == commits of A plus commits of B; assert GET A .dependants == []

criteria.condition: an explicit depends_on is accepted, the lower change's head is not an ancestor of the change's head, and the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is true
criteria.action: record a pending restack of the change onto the lower change's head in the same transaction as the link, and let the background worker run it with trigger manual
criteria.contract: after the worker runs, the change has a new version of kind restack with created_by.actor_type system and base_sha equal to the lower change's head; parley.change.restack carries trigger manual

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: A and B are both built on main and touch different files; PATCH B {depends_on: A}; assert a pending restack for B exists; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.base_sha == A.head_sha; assert isAncestor(A.head_sha, B.head_sha); assert last event of type parley.change.restack has metadata.trigger == 'manual'

criteria.condition: the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is false and an explicit depends_on is accepted whose lower change's head is not an ancestor of the change's head
criteria.action: record no pending restack, move no branch, and set needs_restack to true with restack_reason auto_restack_off on the change
criteria.contract: the change object has needs_restack true and restack_reason auto_restack_off; its version number and source branch head are unchanged

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: as the check above but with changes.auto_restack false: r = PATCH B {depends_on: A}; assert r.json.needs_restack == true; assert r.json.restack_reason == 'auto_restack_off'; assert no pending restack exists; assert B.version and head(B.source) are unchanged

criteria.condition: a change is opened with an explicit depends_on, and a later version of it is recorded
criteria.action: keep the explicit link for version 1 whatever the commit graph says, and apply the automatic rule to the later version
criteria.contract: after the open, depends_on is the given number; after the later version, depends_on is what the automatic rule yields

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
changes.auto_restack is false, so that no restack moves B between the two steps
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go: A and X are open on main; B's branch is built on X's head; open B with depends_on: A; assert B.depends_on == A.number; push one more commit to B's branch (still on X); assert B.depends_on == X.number

requirements.title: Stack depth limit
requirements.rationale: An unbounded chain makes every push at the bottom cost a rebase per change above; the limit caps that cost without losing a pushed head.

criteria.condition: a recorded version or an accepted explicit depends_on puts a change at a depth (the number of changes in its chain of depends_on links down to a change with none, itself included) above [changes].max_stack_depth
criteria.action: record the version and the link all the same, and set needs_restack to true with restack_reason stack_too_deep on that change, leaving every change at or under the limit unflagged
criteria.contract: the change object past the limit has needs_restack true and restack_reason stack_too_deep, its version is recorded and its depends_on is set; a change at exactly the limit has needs_restack false

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over {max_stack_depth 3 with a chain of 5 opened bottom first: changes 1-3 unflagged, 4 and 5 flagged; the key absent from configuration with a chain of 21: change 20 unflagged, change 21 flagged; max_stack_depth 3 and PATCH depends_on that attaches a change on top of a chain of 3: flagged, answered 200}: for each change assert needs_restack and restack_reason as listed; assert every change has a recorded version 1 and the depends_on of the change below

criteria.condition: a change has restack_reason stack_too_deep
criteria.action: start no restack of that change, and none of any change above it, when a change below it gets a new version or lands
criteria.contract: the too-deep change's source branch head and version number are unchanged, and no pending restack exists for it

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: max_stack_depth 2, chain A, B, C (C flagged); push a new version of A; runPending(); assert latest version of B has kind 'restack'; assert C.version == 1; assert head(C.source) is unchanged; assert no pending restack exists for C; assert C.restack_reason == 'stack_too_deep'

criteria.condition: a link of a too-deep change or of a change below it changes so that the change's depth is at or under [changes].max_stack_depth
criteria.action: clear needs_restack and restack_reason on it and, when its head does not have the head of the change below as an ancestor, record a pending restack for it (or set restack_reason auto_restack_off when changes.auto_restack is false)
criteria.contract: the change object has needs_restack false and restack_reason null once it sits on the head below

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: max_stack_depth 2, chain A, B, C (C flagged); push a new version of A and runPending() (B restacked, C untouched); move main to a landed commit that holds A's patch, mark A landed through the store, call the landing entry point for A with a landed commit on main and runPending(); assert B.depends_on == null; assert C.needs_restack == false; assert C.restack_reason == null; assert latest version of C has kind 'restack' and base_sha == B.head_sha

criteria.condition: the configuration sets [changes].max_stack_depth to a value below 1
criteria.action: refuse to start
criteria.contract: the server process exits with status 1 and writes one error line naming changes.max_stack_depth to stderr; it never listens

check.pseudocode: in internal/config/config_test.go, a table over max_stack_depth {0, -1}: err = Load(file); assert err != nil; assert err message contains 'changes.max_stack_depth'. And over {1, 20, 500}: assert err == nil and cfg.Changes.MaxStackDepth == the value; with the key absent assert the value is 20

requirements.title: Restack on a new version below
requirements.rationale: The agent that amends the bottom of a stack should find the changes above it rebased without doing anything.

criteria.condition: a change that has direct dependants gets a new version while the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is true
criteria.action: record one pending restack per direct dependant in the same transaction as the version, and answer the push or commit that caused the version without running any of them
criteria.contract: when the triggering request has been answered, a pending restack exists for each direct dependant and each dependant's source branch head and version number are still what they were

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go: A with dependants B and C (both on A); record a new version of A with the worker stopped; assert pending restacks == {B, C}; assert B.version == 1 and C.version == 1; assert head(B.source) and head(C.source) are unchanged; and with a store that fails the pending write, assert the version of A is not recorded either

criteria.condition: the worker runs a pending restack for a dependant whose head does not have the new head of the change below as an ancestor, and the replay of the dependant's commits applies
criteria.action: move the dependant's source branch with a compare-and-swap to the replayed commits and record a version of kind restack with created_by.actor_type system, base_sha equal to the new head below, the session_id of the version it replaces, and patch_equivalent_to naming the previous version when the diff against its base is identical; clear needs_restack and remove the pending record
criteria.contract: the dependant has a new version {kind: restack, created_by.actor_type: system, base_sha: <new head below>}; its source branch head equals that version's head_sha, which has the new head below as its ancestor; needs_restack is false

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: B (1 commit touching b.txt, session s1) depends on A; amend A (touching a.txt) and record its version; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.number == 2; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.created_by.actor_type == 'system'; assert v.base_sha == A.head_sha; assert v.session_id == 's1'; assert v.patch_equivalent_to == 1; assert head(B.source) == v.head_sha; assert isAncestor(A.head_sha, v.head_sha); assert B.needs_restack == false; assert no pending restack exists

criteria.condition: the hub records a restack version on its own after a new version below
criteria.action: emit parley.change.version with kind restack and then parley.change.restack with onto_sha set to the new head below and trigger version, both with actor system and with ref, version and head_sha of the dependant in the metadata
criteria.contract: two events in this order for the dependant: parley.change.version {kind: restack}, parley.change.restack {onto_sha, trigger: version}; actor system; resource_type change; resource_id the change number

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, in the scenario of the check above with the event log of package 52: evs = events for resource B after the amend; assert types(evs) == ['parley.change.version', 'parley.change.restack']; assert evs[0].metadata.kind == 'restack'; assert evs[1].metadata.onto_sha == A.head_sha; assert evs[1].metadata.trigger == 'version'; assert both have actor system, metadata.version == 2 and metadata.head_sha == B.head_sha

criteria.condition: a restack version is recorded for a change that itself has dependants
criteria.action: restack those dependants in the same way, so that the work continues up the stack bottom first
criteria.contract: every change above the amended one ends with a restack version whose base_sha is the current head of the change directly below it

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: chain A, B, C, D, each one commit on a file of its own; amend A; runPending() until no pending restack is left; for X in (B, C, D): assert latest version of X has kind 'restack' and base_sha == head_sha of the change below; assert the restack events were written in the order B, C, D

criteria.condition: the worker runs a pending restack for a dependant whose head already has the new head of the change below as an ancestor
criteria.action: record no version, emit no event, clear a needs_restack flag whose reason is conflict or auto_restack_off, and remove the pending record
criteria.contract: the dependant's version number and source branch head are unchanged; no parley.change.version or parley.change.restack event is written for it

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: B depends on A; the author rebases B onto A's amended head and pushes it before the worker runs; runPending(); assert B.version == 2 and its kind is 'push'; assert no event of type parley.change.restack exists for B; assert no pending restack exists

criteria.condition: the dependant's source branch moved between the hub reading its head and the compare-and-swap
criteria.action: run the restack again on the new head, at most 5 attempts in one run
criteria.contract: the restack version's head contains the commit that was pushed in between, replayed onto the new head below

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, with a hook that pushes one more commit to B's source branch after the first read of its head: amend A; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert the commits after v.base_sha have the subjects of B's original commit and of the commit pushed in between; assert head(B.source) == v.head_sha

criteria.condition: the compare-and-swap of a background restack is lost 5 times in one run
criteria.action: stop the run, change nothing and keep the pending record
criteria.contract: no restack version and no parley.change.restack event exist for the dependant; its needs_restack is unchanged; the pending record is still present

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, with a hook that moves B's source branch before every compare-and-swap: amend A; runPending(); assert the rebase ran exactly 5 times; assert no version of kind 'restack' exists for B; assert a pending restack for B exists; assert no parley.change.restack event exists for B

criteria.action: for any restack, replay exactly the commits after the change's base_sha up to its head, in order, including when the change below was force-pushed to a head unrelated to its previous one
criteria.contract: the new version has the same number of commits after its base_sha as the old one, with the same subjects and the same patches

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: B has 3 commits on top of A; A's branch is force-pushed to a new commit created from main that shares none of A's old commits and touches other files; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert count(v.base_sha..v.head_sha) == 3; assert their subjects equal B's original subjects in order; assert git patch-id of each equals the original's; assert none of A's old commits is an ancestor of v.head_sha

requirements.title: Restack on landing and on reparenting
requirements.rationale: When the bottom of a stack lands or is abandoned, the next change must sit on what replaced it, not on commits that are no longer a change.

criteria.condition: the landing entry point is called for a change that landed with a landed commit on the target, and changes.auto_restack is true
criteria.action: in one transaction, clear depends_on of each direct dependant and record a pending restack of it onto the landed commit; record nothing when the landed change has no dependants
criteria.contract: each direct dependant has depends_on null and a pending restack whose onto commit is the landed commit

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go: chain A, B, C; move main to a landed commit L that holds A's patch and mark A landed through the store; OnLanded(A, L) with the worker stopped; assert B.depends_on == null; assert pending restacks == {B onto L}; assert C.depends_on == B.number. Second row: OnLanded for a change without dependants; assert no pending restack exists

criteria.condition: the worker runs a pending restack onto a landed commit and the replay of the dependant's commits applies
criteria.action: move the dependant's source branch with a compare-and-swap, record a restack version whose base_sha is the landed commit, and emit parley.change.version and then parley.change.restack with onto_sha equal to the landed commit and trigger land
criteria.contract: the dependant has depends_on null and a new version {kind: restack, base_sha: <landed commit>}; parley.change.restack carries trigger land

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, continuing the scenario above: runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.base_sha == L; assert count(v.base_sha..v.head_sha) == number of B's own commits; assert the last parley.change.restack event for B has metadata.onto_sha == L and metadata.trigger == 'land'

criteria.condition: a direct dependant of a landed change has been restacked and has dependants of its own
criteria.action: keep the depends_on of the changes further up and restack them in turn onto the new head of the change directly below
criteria.contract: a change two levels above the landed one still has depends_on naming the change directly below it, and a restack version whose base_sha is that change's new head

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, continuing the scenario above until no pending restack is left: assert C.depends_on == B.number; v = latest version of C; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.base_sha == B.head_sha; assert isAncestor(L, v.head_sha)

criteria.condition: the abandon of package 23, called with dependants=reparent, has set a direct dependant's depends_on to the abandoned change's depends_on and asks the Restacker interface, which this package implements, to restack that dependant with trigger abandon
criteria.action: record a pending restack of the dependant in the transaction it is given and restack it onto the head of the change it now depends on, or onto the current head of the target branch when there is none, replaying only the dependant's own commits; emit parley.change.restack with trigger abandon
criteria.contract: each dependant's new version has none of the abandoned change's commits among its ancestors; its depends_on is the one package 23 set (the abandoned change's former depends_on) and this package does not write it; parley.change.restack carries trigger abandon; with changes.auto_restack false the dependant gets needs_restack true with restack_reason auto_restack_off and no pending restack

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, a table over {chain A, B, C with B abandoned: C.depends_on == A.number and C's restack version has base_sha == A.head_sha; chain A, B with A abandoned: B.depends_on == null and B's restack version has base_sha == head(main)}: abandon through the abandon route of package 23 with dependants=reparent; runPending(); assert the listed values; assert no commit of the abandoned change is an ancestor of the dependant's head; assert the last parley.change.restack event has metadata.trigger == 'abandon'

requirements.title: Restack failure
requirements.rationale: A conflict must be visible on the change as data and must never leave a branch half rebased.

criteria.condition: the replay of a change's commits in a restack conflicts
criteria.action: move no branch for that change, set needs_restack to true with restack_reason conflict, set mergeable to conflict and conflict to the conflict report through the storing function of package 23, for the pair of the change's head and the commit replayed onto, and remove the pending record
criteria.contract: the change object has needs_restack true, restack_reason conflict, mergeable conflict and a non-null conflict; its version number and source branch head are unchanged

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: A and B (on A) both edit line 1 of f.txt; amend A to rewrite line 1 again; runPending(); assert B.needs_restack == true; assert B.restack_reason == 'conflict'; assert B.mergeable == 'conflict'; assert B.conflict != null; assert B.version == 1; assert head(B.source) is unchanged; assert no pending restack exists; assert no worktree or temporary ref of the rebase is left in the repository

criteria.condition: a restack conflicts for a change that has dependants
criteria.action: start no restack for any change above it
criteria.contract: every change above keeps its version number, its source branch head and needs_restack false; no pending restack exists for it

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go: chain A, B, C where the amend of A conflicts with B and C touches another file; runPending(); assert C.version == 1; assert head(C.source) is unchanged; assert C.needs_restack == false; assert C.depends_on == B.number; assert no pending restack exists

criteria.condition: a restack of a change fails with a conflict and the change was not already in conflict
criteria.action: have the storing function of package 23 emit parley.change.conflict with actor system and metadata files (the conflicted paths) and needs_restack true, by setting the flag before calling it
criteria.contract: one event parley.change.conflict for the change with metadata {files: [paths], needs_restack: true, ref, version, head_sha}

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, in the first scenario of this requirement: evs = events of type parley.change.conflict for B; assert len(evs) == 1; assert evs[0].metadata.files == ['f.txt']; assert evs[0].metadata.needs_restack == true; assert evs[0].actor is system; assert evs[0].metadata.version == 1

criteria.condition: a restack fails with a conflict for a change that already has needs_restack true with restack_reason conflict
criteria.action: replace the stored conflict report with the new one through the storing function of package 23, which emits no further parley.change.conflict event
criteria.contract: the count of parley.change.conflict events for the change stays 1; conflict.target_sha is the newest head below

setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
check.pseudocode: in internal/change/restack_test.go, continuing the first scenario: amend A a second time, again conflicting; runPending(); assert count(events of type parley.change.conflict for B) == 1; assert B.conflict.target_sha == A.head_sha
